scenario: A btrfs mount at /a (qgroups absent) and a nested xfs usrquota mount at /a/b; the queried path /a/bc is a child of /a but not of /a/b, so it must resolve to the /a mount (btrfs, quota disabled) and not to the /a/b mount (xfs, quota enabled).

fixture.mountinfo:
28 28 8:2 / / rw,relatime shared:1 - ext4 /dev/sda2 rw,errors=remount-ro
30 28 0:30 /@a /a rw,relatime shared:2 - btrfs /dev/sdb1 rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=256,subvol=/@a
31 30 259:1 / /a/b rw,relatime shared:3 - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p1 rw,attr2,inode64,usrquota

rationale: Mount resolution rule (contract section C2, 'Mount resolution (per path)'): 'Candidate mounts: mount point equals realpath, or is /, or realpath starts with mount point + /.' For realpath /a/bc the mount point /a qualifies because '/a/bc' starts with '/a/'; the mount point /a/b does NOT qualify, because '/a/bc' does not start with '/a/b/' ('/a/bc' is not inside /a/b, it is a sibling directory whose name merely starts with the characters 'b'). '/' also qualifies but '/a' is the longest mount point, so the chosen mount is the btrfs mount at /a (fstype btrfs, source /dev/sdb1); the nested xfs mount at /a/b is not chosen. Device-check rule: 'If chosen fstype is not btrfs and its major:minor != the path's st_dev -> unknown basis device_mismatch. For btrfs a mismatch is expected (per-subvolume anonymous st_dev, S081) and is recorded as device_check: btrfs_subvolume_skipped.' Here fstype is btrfs and the mount major:minor 0:30 differs from st_dev 0:57 (the btrfs superblock device versus the subvolume's anonymous device), so the path proceeds to quota classification on the btrfs row. btrfs rows: 'source basename maps to exactly one uuid whose qgroups is true -> enabled'; '... exactly one uuid, qgroups false -> disabled | n/a | btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent'; 'zero or several uuids list the device -> unknown | n/a | btrfs_device_unmapped'. The source basename of /dev/sdb1 is sdb1; exactly one uuid (7c3f2a1e-9b4d-4c8a-8f61-2e5d0a7b9c33) lists sdb1 and its qgroups is false, so quota_state disabled, enforcement n/a, basis btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent. The second uuid (d41a9f60-3c72-4e15-9b8a-6f0c2e7d4a81) lists dm-0 and has qgroups true; it is a different device and must not contribute. Verdict precedence: 'setup error -> 2 QUOTA_SETUP; else any enabled -> 1 QUOTA_ENABLED; else any unknown -> 2 QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN; else 0 QUOTA_DISABLED.' The fixture is well formed, the single path is disabled and no path is enabled or unknown, so exit 0 with finding_id QUOTA_DISABLED. Discriminating trap: the /a/b mount carries the xfs super option usrquota, which by the xfs rows ('any of usrquota,uquota,quota,grpquota,gquota,prjquota,pquota and no noquota -> enabled | enforced | xfs_quota_option') would yield enabled/enforced/xfs_quota_option if the implementation wrongly resolved /a/bc to /a/b; the root '/' ext4 mount has no quota option and would yield unknown (basis device_mismatch, since its 8:2 differs from st_dev 0:57 and the contract's device check precedes quota classification; basis ext_quota_superblock_unobservable if the device check is skipped) if '/' were chosen instead of the longer '/a', which in either reading is exit 2 QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN and therefore still distinct from the expected exit 0. Sources: S082 Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst section 3.5 (mountinfo field layout (1)..(m+4), separator field, super options as the last field, optional fields such as shared:N to be ignored); S081 fs/btrfs/inode.c btrfs_getattr stat->dev = BTRFS_I(inode)->root->anon_dev (a btrfs path reports the subvolume anonymous device, so the mount major:minor and the path st_dev differ by design); S079 fs/btrfs/sysfs.c (the qgroups sysfs group under /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>/qgroups/ with its enabled and mode attributes, and the <uuid>/devices/ entries named after the kernel disk name, e.g. sdb1 or dm-0); S080 fs/btrfs/qgroup.c (btrfs_sysfs_add_qgroups/btrfs_sysfs_del_qgroups: the qgroups surface exists only while qgroup support is on, so its absence is the disable signal and its presence the enable signal); S077 Documentation/admin-guide/xfs.rst (uquota/usrquota/uqnoenforce/quota, gquota/grpquota/gqnoenforce, pquota/prjquota/pqnoenforce and noquota are the XFS quota mount options) and S078 fs/xfs/xfs_super.c xfs_fs_show_options (the kernel emits ',usrquota' when XFS_UQUOTA_ENFD and ',noquota' only when no accounting flag is set, so 'rw,attr2,inode64,usrquota' is a kernel-emittable super option string for an enforced user quota).
